Patients in Myrskylä live 96 km by road from HUS Syöpäkeskus in Helsinki, so a 15-session breast course means 16 round trips [S36, S60, S59].

1. The head of radiotherapy at HUS Syöpäkeskus could evaluate a single 8 Gy session as the default for uncomplicated painful bone metastases, with equal pain relief but more retreatment [S31, S30, S62]. Within 30 days, the clinical team reviews its bone metastasis schedules to decide on this default, serving the indicator "National targets and key effectiveness indicators defined for agreed cancers" [S61].

2. The clinical lead for breast radiotherapy could evaluate 5 sessions as the default for eligible patients (whole breast or chest wall without nodal radiotherapy), which is non-inferior to 15 sessions and suits patients for whom distance is a reason to choose it [S9, S11, S15, S60]. Within 30 days, the clinical lead and the clinical team decide whether to adopt this default, serving the indicator "Patients receive treatment within target times" [S24, S25].

3. The director of cancer services could evaluate publishing schedule mix and radiotherapy use by distance band every year, since palliative radiotherapy is used less beyond 100 km from the nearest unit [S21, S29]. Within 30 days, the director of cancer services and the clinical team decide which data to compile, serving the indicator "Regional differences in treatment are available and used to steer services (cross-cutting indicator)" [S26].

Distances are road km from centre points, and the current schedule mix is unknown [S59, S60, S16].

3. The data lead for cancer services could propose publishing schedule mix and radiotherapy use by distance band every year [S26, S21]. This serves "Regional differences in treatment are available and used to steer services (cross-cutting indicator)" [S26].
